definition: Convene means to call a group together for a meeting.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word convene. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know convene should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: When frost took half the seedlings, the co-op president convened an emergency growers' meeting in the seed barn.
Invite is gentler than convene: an invitation asks and waits while every guest is free to say no, but when a chair convenes a committee, the meeting is officially called and members are expected.
Summon goes further than convene — a convened panel is called into session; a summoned witness must appear, ready or not, or answer for the failure.

Gather is the plain, all-purpose verb for coming or bringing together — friends, firewood, a crowd — with no authority implied on either side. Convene is official: someone with standing calls a body into session, and the meeting exists because that call was made.

Assemble means to bring people or parts together into one working whole — a cast, a crew, volunteers on a Saturday. It needs no office behind it; anyone can assemble a team. To convene is narrower: officially calling a deliberative body into session in the first place.
